content.title: About
content.content: Atlantic salmon raised on farms is a tender raw fillet obtained from fish cultivated in controlled freshwater environments. It has a characteristic pink hue, a soft texture, and the rich flavor typical of salmon.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is fully farmed in freshwater and does not migrate to the ocean like many wild species.
Farmed salmon are fed a balanced diet that includes fish oil and plant proteins, resulting in high levels of omega‑3 fatty acids.
Raw salmon is commonly used in sushi, sashimi, and marinated dishes, preserving all its nutrients.
Compared with wild salmon, farmed fish have a more uniform size and fillet shape, making kitchen preparation easier.
Atlantic farmed salmon is generally more affordable than many wild-caught varieties.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Salmon provides EPA and DHA, which support heart, vascular, and brain health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: The raw fillet supplies all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamin D source
items.content: Salmon is one of the best dietary sources of vitamin D, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Selenium
items.content: Selenium in salmon contributes to antioxidant protection and thyroid function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Including B12, B6, and niacin, which are vital for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contaminant risk
items.content: Farmed salmon may contain trace amounts of antibiotics or pesticides if production standards are not met.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood can experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylactic.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Raw salmon is sometimes lightly salted for preservation, increasing its sodium level.

items.title: Possible parasites
items.content: Although farmed salmon are usually treated, freezing at –20 °C for at least 24 hours is recommended before raw consumption to kill parasites.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw salmon fillet is used in sushi, sashimi, tartare, marinades, and cold salads. Slice it thinly and serve with soy sauce, lemon juice, or ginger for added flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw salmon in an airtight container at 0–2 °C. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C for at least 24 hours. Discard any fillet with a strong ammonia odor or off‑color.
